intro: Everything has a name. Your mom, your dog, your chair and your book all have names. In this unit you learn Spanish names for the people, pets and things around you.
In Spanish, a little word comes before each name. It is el or la, and both mean the. You will learn the -o and -a clue that helps you pick. Then you can say Esta es mi mamá and Es un libro.
bigQuestion: How do el and la help us name the people and things around us?

timeline.t: Say la mamá, el papá and el bebé
Name pets: el perro, el gato, el pez, el pájaro
Learn that el and la both mean the
Use un, una and mi: Esta es mi mamá
Name things at school and at home
Use the -o and -a clue to pick el or la
Ask ¿Qué es? and answer Es un... or Es una...

words.d: the sister; el hermano is the brother
the cat — a pet that says meow
the table — ends in -a, so la

test.why: Hermana ends in -a and goes with la.
A cat says meow. El gato is the cat.
Mi means my. La abuela is the grandma.
Silla goes with la and una: una silla.
Mano ends in -o but uses la: la mano.

test.q: ¿Qué es? It is a dog. You say...
test.why: Perro goes with el and un: Es un perro.

test.q: What do el and la mean?
test.why: El and la both mean the. Un and una mean a.
Día breaks the -a clue. We say el día.

write.prompt: Draw your family or your room. Label three people or things with el or la, like la mamá or el libro. Then say one sentence: Esta es mi... (This is my...).
tips: Check el or la for each word. Look at the last letter.
Remember the rule-breakers: el día and la mano.
Say your labels out loud to a friend.
